text: The following question stood in the name of  Dr Tan Wu Meng –   7 To ask the Minister for Manpower with regard to outsourced employment, to what extent do flexible working arrangements (FWA) incentives apply to (i) the outsourcing entity and (ii) the contractor employing the outsourced worker during the period of such employment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: FWAs enable employees to continue working while meeting their personal and family needs, and are especially important for those who have to take care of young children or elderly family members at home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Employers that provide the option of FWAs are more likely to attract and retain talent in the long run.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: That must be the biggest incentive for employers to extend FWAs to their employees.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: I must thank you for standing up because that is a bit of a blind spot in the far right corner.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: As a context, I will give an example.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: A number of my residents have come forward to me.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: They are working in outsourced companies, for example, in security and as cleaners.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: They face this problem when one of them falls sick, for example, they need kidney dialysis and they need that time off.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: It is very difficult for them to get this arrangement.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Eventually, they need to resign and find another job.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: So, that would be my question: how do we ensure that these companies do not pass the buck to one another?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I think what he has described are genuine real challenges on the ground.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Not every job description or job role is amenable to full flexible work arrangements because it depends on the roles the person has to perform and also the nature of the work.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Indeed, many outsourced workers undertake work that could present challenges for their employers to implement flexible work arrangements.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: These include shift workers, workers in frontline or client-facing roles, such as cleaners, manufacturing operators and service workers.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Ultimately, it is about working together, seeing how we can transform the job into something that is, perhaps, much more automated and productive, and this makes it open to possibilities of flexible work arrangements through the use of technology.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I hope that is something that employers, workers and unions can work together on, to make it possible for all job roles to eventually explore some degree of flexible work arrangements.
